name: Combobox
description: An input that filters a list as you type and picks one option: a city, a customer, a time zone, a product. The WAI-ARIA combobox pattern, with the list as a popover under the input.

classes.ayy-combobox: Wrapper: the .ayy-input (role="combobox"), a chevron <svg> and the listbox.
classes.ayy-combobox__listbox: The <ul role="listbox" popover="manual"> of options, placed under the input.
classes.ayy-combobox__option: An <li role="option">. data-value is what it stands for, data-label what goes in the input, data-keywords more words that match. aria-selected="true" on the one the arrow keys are on; aria-disabled for one you can't pick.
classes.ayy-combobox__meta: Extra text at the end of an option (a country, a count). Not put in the input.
classes.ayy-combobox__empty: The "No matches" line (role="none"), shown when nothing matches.

default.looks: An Input with a muted chevron at the inline end; the list is a raised popover with the overlay shadow.

hover.looks: Option gets the wash-hover background (the input hovers like Input).

pressed.none: Options have no pressed look: clicking picks one and closes the list.

focus.looks: Input's ring. Focus stays in the input while the arrow keys move through options (see selected).

disabled.looks: Option dims to --ayy-opacity-disabled with a not-allowed cursor; a disabled input dims like Input.

selected.looks: The option under the arrow keys gets the wash-hover background. Forced colours: Highlight fill.

loading.none: No loading look; while results load, show .ayy-combobox__empty with "Searching…".

open.looks: The list fades in under the input, at most 18rem (or half the viewport) tall, then scrolls.

empty.looks: Muted "No results" row when every option is filtered out.

sizes.density: Input height and options (md control height, 32px compact, 40 comfortable, 44 touch) follow data-density.
sizes.width: Fills its container; the list is at most 28rem wide.

js: connectCombobox(input, listbox, { onSelect?, filter? }) → { open, close, refresh, destroy } wires the pattern on plain markup; comboboxOptionLabel(option) and comboboxOptionByValue(listbox, value) read options; comboboxChevronIcon (SVG markup) and part class constants.

element.description: Wraps an .ayy-combobox and wires typing, filtering, the arrow keys, Enter and Esc on its input and listbox.

attributes.manual: Don't filter: replace the options yourself as people type (a search API), then call refresh().

events.ayy-select: { value, label, option } when an option is chosen — value is its data-value, else its label.

props.options: ({ value, label, meta?, icon?, keywords?, disabled? } | string)[]
props.onInputChange: (text: string) => void — every keystroke, e.g. to fetch options
props.filter: boolean, default true; false when you fetch the options yourself
props.name: string — a hidden input carries the chosen value in forms

a11y: Focus stays in the input: Down opens the list and moves through it, Up goes back, Enter picks, Esc closes (and a second Esc clears), Alt+Down opens without moving. Screen readers follow aria-activedescendant.
Label the input with a <label for> its id; the chevron is decoration.
Typing highlights the first match, so Enter picks it; options that don't match are hidden, and "No matches" shows when none do.
do: Use a combobox to pick one of many known values: more than ten or so, where people know what they're looking for (a city, a customer, a time zone).
Give options keywords for the other words people type (the country for a city, the email for a customer), and meta for what helps tell them apart.
For results from a server, set filter={false} (or manual on <ayy-combobox>) and replace the options on each keystroke.
dont: Don't use a combobox for fewer than about ten options — use Select, or a Segmented control for two to five.
Don't use it for actions — use a Dropdown menu.
Don't use it for free text that may not be in the list — use an Input (a datalist can suggest).
